topline.text: Alan Milburn's long-awaited final review into youth inactivity has been published, calling for a legal 'Young People's Guarantee' - a route into work, education or training for every under-25. His interim findings found SEND pupils roughly 80% more likely to become NEET than their peers.
topline.action: Could usefully inform post-16 transition planning conversations for SEND cohorts.

topline.text: Government signals possible concessions on SEND reform - reportedly weighing new routes (an ombudsman or independent review panel) for families to challenge support decisions, after backlash over plans to remove Tribunal access for most pupils.
Last call: DfE's call for evidence on exclusion reform (internal suspension, reintegration partnerships, schoolwork during suspension) closes tomorrow, 19 November.
topline.action: Last chance for any Sheffield-side input before tomorrow's deadline.

items.lede: Milburn's final NEET review calls for a legal 'Young People's Guarantee'.
items.body: The long-delayed final report from Alan Milburn's review into youth inactivity proposes a legal duty on government to guarantee under-25s a route into work, education or training, modelled on local authorities' existing duties toward homeless people. It builds on his May interim report, which found young people with SEND are around 80% more likely to be NEET than their peers - a gap Milburn says needs addressing earlier than the post-16 transition point. Coverage cites a multi-billion-pound funding package attached to the plan, but the exact figure isn't yet corroborated across other reporting, so treat any number with caution until DfE confirms it.
items.action: Worth a look for anyone shaping post-16 transition or careers provision for SEND pupils.

items.lede: Ministers reportedly weighing concessions on SEND appeal rights.
items.body: Amid continued backlash over plans to replace most EHCPs with Individual Support Plans - which, as proposed, would remove access to the independent SEND Tribunal for anyone below the top support tier - government sources suggest new appeal routes, potentially an ombudsman or independent review panel, are now under consideration. Campaigners are pushing for firm guarantees before the Education for All Bill, which isn't expected until early 2027.
items.source: Independent Schools Council daily news summary

items.lede: Exclusion reform call for evidence closes tomorrow.
items.body: The DfE's call for evidence on behaviour management - covering internal suspension, reintegration support partnerships and schoolwork provision during the first days of a suspension or exclusion - closes 19 November. It feeds proposals in the 'Every Child Achieving and Thriving' white paper for a time-limited internal suspension framework.
items.action: Last chance for any Sheffield-side input before tomorrow's deadline.
